source.title: UniMixer: A Unified Architecture for Scaling Laws in Recommendation Systems
source.authors: Mingming Ha; Guan-Chen Wang; Lin-Xun Chen; Xuan Rao; Yue-Xin Shi; Tian-Bao Ma; Zhao-Jie Liu; Yunqian Fan; Zi-Long Lu; Ya-Nan Niu; Hanlin Li; Kun Gai

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling in supervised recommendation models, a different task setting from language-model pretraining, and reports AUC scaling curves.
record.gate_note: The study reports fitted AUC power laws versus parameters and FLOPs for three recommendation architectures. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit small-run curves to predict much larger runs, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Other results, including the online CAD gains and ablations, do not measure the power-law behavior in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of AUC gain against dense parameters and FLOPs for three recommendation architectures, including the external RankMixer baseline. That is a result on whether the power-law form holds outside text pretraining (V5). Its main aim is proposing an architecture, and the evidence is thin: about one decade of scale, no uncertainty, and ΔAUC rather than loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report that AUC shows clear power-law trends in parameters and FLOPs for all three architectures, and that UniMixer-Lite has the largest exponent and coefficient. They also claim depth scaling beats width scaling for UniMixer while RankMixer degrades with depth, and report >15% online CAD gains. They frame these mainly as evidence for their unified architecture.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised recommendation-model scaling measured by AUC, rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy; varies model parameters and FLOPs and does not test compute-optimal parameter/token splits.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponents differ across the three architectures and between parameter-count and FLOPs scaling.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is for recommendation AUC rather than language-model held-out loss. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the fitted scaling laws or exact parameter/FLOPs ranges for the curves.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-curve equations are reported beyond the six fits in Section 5.2. Results on online CAD, ablations, and architecture depth are omitted because they do not measure the power-law outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
No fixed-compute parameter/data allocation; data size never varied.
Depth vs width is compared only qualitatively (Fig. 6) and not at a fixed parameter count.
No data-size scaling, no loss as measure, and only about one decade of model size. Image/video, repeated data and fine-tuning are not tested.
No downstream prediction from loss or scale. The online CAD gain is not a scaling curve.
No fitting-method or schedule sensitivity. Exponents only differ by architecture.

missing.what: Depth-scaling results: RankMixer 2→4 blocks drops AUC by 0.1066% (4.44M→8.66M params). UniMixer-Lite 2/4/8 blocks gives +0.1575% then +0.1647%, a near plateau.

record.verdict_notes: The measure is ΔAUC on a binary user-retention task, not cross-entropy loss. Only model size/compute is varied; data size is fixed at about 0.7B samples. Exponent differences across architectures are architecture-dependence rather than fitting-choice dependence, so no V7 label is given.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss or cross-entropy measurements.
No test of predictions from small runs against substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute optimization of parameter and token allocation.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at a fixed parameter count.
Tests recommendation models using AUC, not language-model held-out loss. Does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Does not test downstream task performance as predicted by language-model pretraining loss or scale.
Does not investigate sensitivity of exponents or compute-optimal allocations to fitting choices, schedules, data, or parameter counting.

relationships.condition: RankMixer, UniMixer, UniMixer-Lite (2 blocks); Kuaishou user-retention data; ΔAUC vs dense params and FLOPs over ~1 decade
relationships.reason: All six fits are power laws, with exponents of about 0.12–0.14 (r1–r6). Range is narrow and no fit quality is reported.
relationships.display_finding: All six parameter and compute fits followed power laws with exponents approximately 0.12–0.14, although the range was narrow and fit quality was unreported.

relationships.condition: Scaling along depth: RankMixer 2→4 blocks; UniMixer-Lite 4→8 blocks (Table 4)
relationships.reason: From the text, not rows. RankMixer AUC falls 0.1066% when parameters roughly double. UniMixer-Lite gains only 0.0072 points from 4 to 8 blocks. So the power-law gain depends on architecture and scaling axis.
relationships.display_finding: Roughly doubling RankMixer parameters reduced AUC by 0.1066%, while increasing UniMixer-Lite from four to eight blocks gained only 0.0072 points.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RankMixer, UniMixer, and UniMixer-Lite on Kuaishou user-retention recommendation data; AUC versus parameters and FLOPs
reader_labels.reason: All six reported fits are power laws, which supports power-law scaling in this tested recommendation setting (r1–r6). This is AUC evidence, not evidence about language-model cross-entropy.
